title: Greenfield Rust expression evaluator: tokenize, parse, and evaluate arithmetic expressions
description: Build a Rust library from scratch that tokenizes, parses, and evaluates simple arithmetic expressions with +, -, *, / and parentheses.

task_spec.prompt:
Create a Rust expression evaluator library in src/lib.rs.

Implement:

pub fn eval(expr: &str) -> Result<f64, String>
  Evaluates a string arithmetic expression and returns the result.
  Supported: integer and decimal literals, +, -, *, / operators, parentheses, and whitespace.
  Operator precedence: * and / bind tighter than + and -.
  Returns Err(msg) for division by zero, unbalanced parentheses, or invalid tokens.
  Examples:
    eval("2 + 3") == Ok(5.0)
    eval("10 / 2 * 3") == Ok(15.0)
    eval("(1 + 2) * (3 + 4)") == Ok(21.0)
    eval("1 / 0") == Err(...)
    eval("((1 + 2)") == Err(...)

Write at least 8 tests covering: addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, mixed precedence, parentheses, division-by-zero error, unbalanced-paren error.

Use recursive descent parsing — do not use any external crates. cargo test must pass all 8+ tests. cargo build must succeed.
required_artifacts: 8+ tests covering all operators, precedence, parens, and error cases
followup_prompts: Run `cargo test` and show me which tests are passing and which are still failing. Fix any failures — pay attention to edge cases like empty input, boundary values, and error conditions.
Final check: run `cargo test` one more time. All tests must be green. If anything is still failing, trace through the failing assertion and fix it now.
